title: Token-leg retry depends on the launch token refunding the repeat storage_deposit (0.00125 NEAR)
status: DISCLOSED, bounded (sandbox measured; real factory token repeat-refund not probed)
summary: Sandbox test tests/tests/instant_token_leg_storage.rs, record evidence/instant-n04/storage-deposit-retry.json. Every token-leg attempt attaches 0.00125 NEAR of the launcher's own balance to storage_deposit(market). Against a NEP-145 token that refunds a repeat deposit, a retry changes the launcher's NEAR balance by 0 (measured -1e-24 NEAR, the one attached yocto). Against a token that KEEPS the deposit, each retry costs the launcher exactly 0.00125 NEAR (3 of 3 retries measured). The first attempt always pays the real registration once. Worst case, exact: a retry exists only after a refused token leg (market paused or misconfigured, token ft_transfer_call refused), and open_instant is permissionless with no cooldown, so while refusals last anyone can repeat it; each repeat moves 0.00125 NEAR out of the launcher's pooled NEAR (the per-launch deposits that fund record storage, the market storage forward and refunds), about 800 retries per 1 NEAR, until the launcher balance reaches its storage-staking floor. The sender burns about 0.00135 NEAR of gas per retry against the cheapest possible receiver (stub market, about 13.5 Tgas) and more against the real market, so the drain costs the attacker at least as much as it takes: griefing at cost parity, never a profit. Not proven: that the real testnet or mainnet factory token refunds a repeat deposit. Its bounds are min 0.00125 = max 0.00125 NEAR (docs/runbooks/instant-testnet.md), so NEP-145 requires the refund; confirm with one repeat storage_deposit on testnet when a testnet transaction is allowed. Mitigation if it matters: attach the registration deposit once per launch (a flag like market_prepared), which needs a launcher change and a redeploy.

title: Who controls test.near, testnet and localnet on mainnet (profile suffix rule)
summary: Read-only mainnet RPC (rpc.mainnet.fastnear.com, view_account and view_access_key_list, 2026-11-10, blocks 223838969 to 223838972, no key, no write). test.near EXISTS: 34.558 NEAR, no contract (code_hash is all ones), one FullAccess key (ed25519:8fohZQ3DwXgVUXKJSoU9vi6iPyXKUKKff1T7sw4xj4wW) and three function-call keys limited to __wallet__metadata on test.near. Whoever holds that one full-access key can create any X.test.near on mainnet, and the launcher's testnet and demo profiles accept an account that ends .test.near, so only that key holder could deploy a lookalike launcher with the demo profile (10 second days) at a .test.near name on mainnet. testnet does NOT exist on mainnet (UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT, no keys) and localnet does NOT exist (UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT, no keys). Both are top-level names, and a top-level name shorter than 32 characters can be created only by the registrar account, so nobody can create X.testnet or X.localnet on mainnet today. Bound: the mainnet profile requires a .near account and rejects .testnet and .localnet, a lookalike would sit under someone else's account name, and it cannot touch the real launcher, whose account is checked at init (R_PROFILE). Residual: users must trust only the exact launcher account the app names. Optional hardening: drop the .test.near suffix from the testnet and demo accept list once the sandbox tests no longer need it.
